body: Model: a firm that passes its scale savings back to customers (lower prices, better service) grows volume faster, which deepens scale advantages, which allows more sharing - a flywheel competitors without scale cannot match. Costco (low fixed markups, membership fees) and Amazon (prices, free shipping, reinvestment) were Nomad's archetypes. Tools: (1) destination analysis - estimate what the business looks like in 10-20 years and whether today's price reflects it; (2) judge management by whether they sacrifice near-term margin for customer value; (3) concentrate in the best 3-10 ideas and hold through noise; (4) avoid 'scale economies kept' (firms raising prices on captive customers), which invites competition and regulation. Indian candidates for the test: discount retail, low-cost brokers/AMCs, platform businesses, airlines with cost leadership - but verify the customer-value claim with data (prices vs competitors, volume share).
title: Sleep/Zakaria: scale economies shared and destination analysis
